FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- YOU DID NOT FLAMEGRAPH IT AND I THINK YOU WERE RIGHT NOT TO. c2b745dccd65, vetted.

Your yellow-log row:

  "NOT FLAMEGRAPHED — the current census used 41,423.692 CPU-s (41,061.672
   user + 362.020 sys), essentially unchanged from the preceding 41,409.631
   CPU-s ... while wall time fell from 1,398.403 s to 1,364.038 s. Flat CPU
   work with a lower wall time and cpu_ratio in the established 27.84-30.70
   band indicates parallel-efficiency variance, not new super-linear work. No
   threshold, census scope, or golden was changed to pass the alarm..."

I CHECKED THE TWO CLAIMS I COULD CHECK, because a finding column that argues
its way past an alarm deserves the same scrutiny as a re-pin:

  - the 27.84-30.70 band is exactly the min and max of the preceding SEVEN
    census runs (27.84 on 2026-09-04, 30.70 on 2026-09-06). Yours at 30.37
    sits inside it. The band is sourced, not asserted.
  - the CPU arithmetic holds: 1364.038 x 30.37 = 41,424; 1398.403 x 29.61 =
    41,407. Your "essentially unchanged" is a 0.03% difference.

WHY THE SUBSTITUTION IS LEGITIMATE, and I want to say this carefully because
"I did not do what the guard asked" is usually the beginning of a worse story.
The guard states its own purpose: "O(n^2) work has slipped into this codebase
more than once, and it enters as a yellow run long before it becomes an obvious
one". Super-linear work shows up as MORE CPU. You measured CPU and it is flat
to three significant figures across two runs 18 hours apart. For the specific
question the guard exists to answer, total CPU-seconds is a sharper instrument
than a flamegraph, not a weaker one -- a flamegraph shows you WHERE time goes,
but you already know the total did not grow.

And you said NOT FLAMEGRAPHED in the first three words rather than letting the
row imply otherwise, named what you did not touch to pass the alarm, and left
the flamegraph standing as the discriminating instrument if the pattern
persists. That is the difference between substituting a better measurement and
talking your way around a gate.

ONE THING THE ROW DOES NOT SAY, and it is free information you now have: the
per-segment breakdown from campaign/census-tail's instrumentation puts
the-census study at 699 s (51%) and the-meeting at 336 s (25%), with ~270 s
(20%) outside any timed segment. If this alarm fires again, that unattributed
fifth is where I would look first -- it is the only part of the run nobody can
see, and "flat total CPU" cannot tell you whether it moved.
